To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantum statistical mechanical properties of a system of n detectors in arbitrary motion interacting with a quantum field, can be described by a set of Langevin equations, and that the statistical correlations of the detectors are described by a set general fluctuation dissipation relations, which are valid for all trajectories, and for arbitrary initial states of detectors, and a set of correlation-propagation relations which are valid for trajectories that do not contain event horizons, and for arbitrary states of motion and initial states of the detectors.

the mutual influence of quantum field detectors on each other is described by a Langevin equation that includes backreaction of the detectors on the quantum field self-consistently; and that there are general fluctuation-dissipation relations and correlation-propagation relations that encapsulate the statistical properties of the quantum field.

the quantum statistical mechanical properties of detectors and fields in arbitrary states of motions are governed by the influence functional method, which contains the backreaction self-consistently, and the resulting Langevin equations can be used to study the statistical mechanical properties, and to derive general fluctuation-dissipation relations and correlation-propagation relations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of quantum statistical properties of systems in arbitrary states of relative motion interacting with quantum fields.
the quantum statistical mechanical properties of detectors in motion.

the quantum statistical properties and the mutual effects of detectors in motion interacting with each another via a quantum field, with the aim of understanding the statistical mechanical properties and the backreaction of quantum fields on moving detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quantum statistical properties (noise, correlations, and dissipation) of detectors and their interactions with quantum fields are fully described by the Langevin equations and the influence functional, which is the quantum statistical mechanical analogue to the classical Hamilton's equations and the Lagrangian.

the quantum statistical properties (e.g. noise and correlation) of accelerated detectors are determined by a combination of three factors: (i) the quantum statistical properties and the trajectory of each individual detector, (ii) the mutual interaction of detectors through the quantum field, and (iii) the quantum statistical nature of the field itself.
the statistical properties of accelerated detectors can be understood by the same methods and ideas that apply to the quantum theory of measurement in a quantum field theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutual impedance and the advanced and retarded noise can be understood as quantum statistical phenomena of particles and fields.
the mutual influence between detectors is important in quantum field theory.

we have developed a systematic method to study the statistical mechanics of quantum fields in the presence of accelerated detectors, which could be used to study the quantum statistical properties in atomic and optical systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quantum statistics of detectors in arbitrary states of motions interacting with each other through a quantum field are fully characterized by a few simple equations, which are the generalization of well-known classical results.

the quantum statistics of accelerated detectors is a rich and interesting subject, and that the quantum statistical properties are not only a function of the acceleration of the detector, but also of the state of motion of the detector.

the statistical mechanical properties, such as the noise, impedance, fluctuation dissipation relations, etc., are all determined by the quantum statistical properties, such as correlations and entropies, and the motion of the detectors.
